title: Proxies and load balancers
summary: What sits between the user and your app, and what it does to requests.

steps.title: The path of a real request
body: browser -> CDN edge -> load balancer -> reverse proxy -> app instance 1
- A **reverse proxy** accepts requests on behalf of servers: terminates TLS, routes by host/path, compresses, adds headers.
- A **load balancer** spreads traffic across healthy instances. **Layer 4** balancers forward TCP/UDP without reading it; **layer 7** balancers read HTTP and can route by path, header or cookie.
- **Health checks** (`GET /health` every few seconds) take broken instances out of rotation.

steps.prompt: Can a layer 4 balancer do it, or does it need layer 7?
items: Send `/api/*` to one pool and `/` to another

steps.title: What the app sees
body: Behind a proxy, the TCP connection your app sees comes **from the proxy**, not the user. The proxy passes the original details in headers:
Each proxy **appends** the address it received the connection from. So the left-most entry is the original client *if* you trust every hop:
anyone can send a fake `X-Forwarded-For` header. The safe way is to walk from the **right**, skipping your own known proxies.
In ASP.NET Core this is `UseForwardedHeaders` with `KnownProxies`/`KnownNetworks`.

steps.prompt: Your app behind a load balancer generates redirect URLs starting `http://` although users use HTTPS, and every log line shows the client IP `10.0.0.7`. Fix?
options: Enable forwarded-headers handling so the app reads `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-For` from the trusted balancer
Turn off HTTPS on the balancer
Give the app a public IP
steps.explain: TLS ends at the balancer, so the app sees plain HTTP from `10.0.0.7`. The forwarded headers restore the original scheme and client.

steps.title: The real client IP
prompt: Write `string ClientIp(string remoteAddress, string? xForwardedFor, HashSet<string> trustedProxies)`.
Build the chain: the addresses in `X-Forwarded-For` (comma-separated, trimmed) followed by `remoteAddress`.
Walk it from the **right**: skip addresses that are trusted proxies; the first untrusted one is the client.
If every address is trusted, return the left-most.
starter: string ClientIp(string remoteAddress, string? xForwardedFor, HashSet<string> trustedProxies)
solution: string ClientIp(string remoteAddress, string? xForwardedFor, HashSet<string> trustedProxies)
template: Dojo.Eq("spoofed left entry ignored", "198.51.100.23", ClientIp("10.0.0.7", "6.6.6.6, 198.51.100.23", dojoT));
hints: Make one list: forwarded entries then the remote address.
Loop from the end; return the first address not in the trusted set.

steps.prompt: Complete the nginx reverse-proxy block so the app sees the original host and scheme.
steps.explain: `proxy_pass` names the upstream; `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for` appends the client to any existing header.

steps.prompt: One of three instances hangs on every request, yet the load balancer keeps sending it a third of the traffic. Its health check is `TCP connect to port 80`. Best fix?
options: Use an HTTP health check on `/health` that exercises the app, with a timeout
steps.explain: A hung process still accepts TCP connections. A layer 7 check with a short timeout notices the app isn't answering.

steps.title: Round robin with health
prompt: Write a class `Balancer` constructed with `List<string> backends`:
- `void MarkDown(string b)` / `void MarkUp(string b)` change health.
- `string? Next()` returns backends in rotation, skipping unhealthy ones; `null` if none is healthy.
The rotation remembers its position: with A, B, C all healthy, `Next()` gives A, B, C, A, ...
If B is down, it gives A, C, A, C.
template: Dojo.Eq("rotation", new List<string?> { "A", "B", "C", "A" }, new List<string?> { dojoB.Next(), dojoB.Next(), dojoB.Next(), dojoB.Next() });
Dojo.Eq("skips B", new List<string?> { "A", "C", "A", "C" }, new List<string?> { dojoB2.Next(), dojoB2.Next(), dojoB2.Next(), dojoB2.Next() });
hints: Keep an index that wraps with `% backends.Count`.
Try at most `backends.Count` times before giving up.
